about: Examples for the numbers that reach back past this week: the streak (days in a row the app was opened),
the trophies, what each past week added up to, the goal offer, and the averages on the Summary page.
The app and the backend each have their own copy of these calculations:
src/lib/rewards.ts, src/lib/goal.ts, src/services/context.ts and src/services/summary.ts in the app,
Two tests read this file and work every example out, one with each copy:
Both have to get what is under `expect` (numbers to 3 decimals). The answers were worked out by hand; `how` shows the reasoning.
When a rule changes on purpose: change both copies, then the answers here.

fields.plan: the 7 days, Monday first, each one of: off | 0 | 5 | 10 | 30 | 45 (minutes). Past weeks use the same plan.
fields.workouts: this week's workouts: day (0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday), met, minutes. A workout from Fitbit also has its Fitbit band (fairly | very) and whether the user confirmed it; one without `confirmed` is confirmed.
fields.opens: the days of this week the app was opened, as day numbers. Today counts whether it is listed or not; days after today don't count.
fields.past_weeks: full weeks before this one, oldest first, so the last one is last week. Each has its own goal, its workouts, and `opens`: the days the app was opened, or null when there is no record of that for the week. An empty list is only for a week with no workouts: the backend keeps opens as dates, so it can't tell 'never opened' from 'no record' and would count that week's workout days.

expect.streak: current: days in a row ending today. best: the longest run so far.
expect.trophies: all trophies so far, this week's included
expect.week_done: MET-hours done this week, up to today
expect.past_done: MET-hours done in each past week
expect.past_opens: for each past week, the days that count as opened (day numbers)
expect.past_active: for each past week, the days with any workout (day numbers)
expect.offer: the goal offer: kind (raise | lower | keep) and the goal it suggests
expect.summary: the Summary page: weeks averaged (up to the last 4), avg_met_hours, avg_brisk_min, goal_weeks, avg_active_days, longest_gap (days in a row with no workout, up to today), and intensity (minutes a week that are light, moderate, vigorous)

examples.name: A new user on their first Monday
examples.how: Today counts as opened, so the streak is 1. There are no past weeks: no trophies, nothing to average, and the goal stays.

examples.name: The streak runs across the weekend into this week, and today counts
examples.how: Last week: Monday, then Tuesday and Wednesday missed, then Thursday to Sunday (4 days). This week: Monday, Tuesday, and today. 4 + 3 = 7 in a row.

examples.name: A missed day starts a new run, and the best run stays on record
examples.how: All of last week plus Monday and Tuesday is 9 days in a row. Wednesday was missed. Thursday and today make 2.

examples.name: A past week with no record of opens uses its workout days
examples.how: Two weeks ago has a record (Monday to Thursday), so its Friday workout doesn't add a day. Last week has none, so Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday count as opened. Saturday, Sunday and today make 3; the best run is the 4 days two weeks ago. Last week: 2.0 + 3.0 + 1.0 = 6.0 MET-hours.

examples.name: Trophies: each week against its own goal, and this week's as soon as it is reached
examples.how: Past weeks did 7.5, 7.0, 11.0 and 10.5 against a goal of 7.5: three trophies (7.5 is exactly enough, 7.0 is not). This week: 6.0 + 4.0 = 10.0 of 10, a fourth. With the goal at 10, the lower of the last two weeks (10.5) rounds down to 10, which is not higher, so the goal stays. Average 36.0 / 4 = 9.0 MET-hours, 180 brisk minutes. Moderate minutes: 90 / 4 = 22.5, shown as 23. Vigorous: 260 / 4 = 65. 28 days opened, then Monday, Tuesday and today.

examples.name: Two strong weeks: the offer is to raise the goal
examples.how: 11.0 and 10.3 MET-hours. The lower one, 10.3, rounded down to a multiple of 2.5 is 10, above the goal of 7.5: raise to 10. Both weeks earned a trophy. Vigorous minutes: 213 / 2 = 106.5, shown as 107.

examples.name: Three weeks under half the goal: the offer is to lower it
examples.how: 3.0, then 2.6 (an unconfirmed Fitbit workout counts at 3.0 MET: 3.0 × 52 / 60), then 3.4 (the 2 MET hour is light and adds nothing). All under 3.75, half the goal: lower to 3.75. Last week's Saturday and Sunday count as opened, then Monday to today: 6 in a row. Minutes a week: light 60 / 3 = 20, moderate 112 / 3 = 37.3, vigorous 34 / 3 = 11.3.

examples.name: Days after today don't count
examples.how: Today is Wednesday. Friday's workout and the opens on Friday and Saturday are after today, so they are left out: 2.5 MET-hours done, and Monday, Tuesday and today make 3 in a row. Tuesday and today have no workout: a gap of 2.

examples.name: A week with nothing in it is a week with nothing done
examples.how: Two weeks ago: opened every day, 7.5 MET-hours, a trophy. Last week: nothing. The run of 7 ended, and today starts a new one. Average (7.5 + 0) / 2 = 3.75 MET-hours, 75 brisk minutes. No workout from that Thursday to today: 4 + 7 + 1 = 12 days.

examples.name: Half a brisk minute rounds up, so the workouts have to be added in order
examples.how: 6.8 + 1.025 + 2.175 + 1.675 = 11.675 MET-hours, which is 233.5 brisk minutes, shown as 234. A sum that corrects its own rounding (Python 3.12's sum()) lands just under 11.675 and shows 233. Vigorous: 60 + 15 + 15 = 90 minutes, moderate 15. Monday to Thursday count as opened; Friday to Sunday don't, so today starts a new run.
